root_cause_label: Heuristic keyword-based fluorophore selection without spectral verification via FPbase
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent selected fluorescent protein donor/acceptor and antibody-binder components using title-keyword heuristics and unverified guesses rather than querying FPbase for exact 505 nm excitation and 610 nm emission matches, producing a gBlock with biologically incorrect components.
t_err_evidence: At step 10 the agent explicitly assigns hard-coded estimated excitation/emission values (490/510 for 'green', 560/600 for 'orange/red') based solely on title keywords, never querying FPbase for actual spectral data; MKO (orange-emitting GFP-like) is misclassified as a donor rather than acceptor, and 4KGE (NIR FP, ~590/670 nm) is catalogued as an acceptor at ~600nm emission—all without any real spectral lookup.
t_commit_evidence: At step 12 the agent explicitly selects specific PDB IDs for all five components: antibody binder = 1AK4 (cyclophilin A, not the antibody target), donor = 5JZL, acceptor = 4KGE (NIR FP, wrong emission), molecule binder = 3KZY. From this point all subsequent steps build exclusively on these wrong choices and no re-evaluation of component identity occurs.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked the domain knowledge that fluorescent protein spectral properties cannot be inferred from name keywords alone, and did not know the specific excitation/emission peaks of proteins like 4KGE (NIR FP, ~590/670 nm) or 3ADF (Azami-Green, ~492/505 nm). When the FPbase API call failed at step 7, the agent resorted to hard-coded heuristic estimates instead of diagnosing and fixing the API call. It also never identified what the antibody in antibody.fasta targets, defaulting to cyclophilin A as 'a stable scaffold.'
forewarning_evidence: At step 7 the FPbase API call returns a JSONDecodeError (empty response body), signalling that the spectral database cannot be queried. Instead of fixing the request, the agent silently proceeds to heuristic matching at steps 8 and 10.
